Short answer
- Root cause: ledger-api processes on rcabench-worker2 exhausted file descriptors (EMFILE / "Too many open files"), causing the app to fail accepts and return 503/connection refused to the readiness probe → kubelet marked those containers NotReady. Affected pods: 3 of 6 (half).

What I found (evidence)
- Pod list (ledger namespace, deployment ledger-api):
  - ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
  - ledger-api-866db84748-cz4wp — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
  - ledger-api-866db84748-vv6jk — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
  - ledger-api-866db84748-md6xh — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker
  - ledger-api-866db84748-r5mbh — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker
  - ledger-api-866db84748-xzjxb — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker

- Deployment rollout to image with APP_VERSION=1.4.2 occurred during the timeframe when these pods were created (new replicaset ledger-api-866db84748 created ~19m ago in the cluster output).

- Pod events show repeated readiness probe failures:
  - Example: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.15:8080/healthz": dial tcp 10.244.1.15:8080: connect: connection refused
  - Later: Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503

- Application logs from the affected pods (logs fetched from last 30 minutes; showing all matched lines; limit=200, filters: error|exception|503|connection refused etc.):
  - Repeated lines (sample):
    2026-10-07T09:45:33Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
    2026-10-07T09:45:43Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files
    ... (repeats every ~10s until ~2026-10-07T09:58:03Z)
  - Total matched error lines per pod: many (the fetch returned ~76 filtered lines per pod)

Why this indicates the root cause
- "[Errno 24] Too many open files" is direct, authoritative evidence that the process hit the per-process file descriptor limit (EMFILE). When the server cannot accept new socket connections it will refuse connections or return 5xx; Kubernetes readiness probes then fail and the pod becomes NotReady. The errors are emitted by the application itself (not a network flake) and align exactly with the readiness-probe failures and the timing of the rollout on rcabench-worker2. Only pods on rcabench-worker2 show the EMFILE errors — the other nodes' pods are healthy.

Possible immediate triggers (hypotheses)
1. Application has an FD leak (not closing sockets / files) introduced or exacerbated by 1.4.2 — likely, because the errors start immediately after the new pods started.
2. Node/container runtime or process ulimit on rcabench-worker2 is unusually low, exposing normal app behaviour to EMFILE only on that node.
3. A sudden spike in incoming connections combined with either of the above.

What to do right now (fast remediation)
1. Restore availability quickly:
   - Option A (safe, fast): Restart the failing pods so they reschedule (they may go to the other worker):
     kubectl delete pod ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -n ledger
     kubectl delete pod ledger-api-866db84748-cz4wp -n ledger
     kubectl delete pod ledger-api-866db84748-vv6jk -n ledger
   - Option B: Rollback the deployment to the previous revision if you suspect 1.4.2 is the cause:
     kubectl rollout undo deployment/ledger-api -n ledger
   - Option C (one-liner to restart whole deployment):
     kubectl rollout restart deployment/ledger-api -n ledger

2. While pods come back, prevent reoccurrence on rcabench-worker2 by cordoning/draining it if needed:
   kubectl cordon rcabench-worker2
   kubectl drain rcabench-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data

Longer-term fixes (next actions)
1. Fix the app (most important)
   - Inspect code for FD leaks: ensure sockets, file descriptors, DB connections, files are closed.
   - Reproduce locally / in staging with high connection rates and monitor open fd count.

2. Add diagnostics to the image
   - In a running pod, count open fds quickly:
     kubectl exec -n ledger <pod> -- sh -c 'ls /proc/1/fd | wc -l'
   - Or (if lsof present): kubectl exec -n ledger <pod> -- lsof -p 1 | wc -l

3. Raise process/container NOFILE as needed
   - Easiest permanent approach: adjust the container entrypoint to set rlimit before starting Python:
     In Dockerfile or entrypoint script:
       ulimit -n 65536
       exec python -u /code/ledger_api.py
   - Alternatively, configure the node/container runtime to set higher LimitNOFILE for containers (systemd/unit override for containerd to set LimitNOFILE, then restart containerd on nodes and recreate pods). Example (on each node):
     - Create systemd drop-in for containerd.service with LimitNOFILE=65536 and restart containerd (requires maintenance window).
   - Also check kernel-wide max (fs.file-max) and increase if needed:
     sysctl -w fs.file-max=200000

4. Monitoring & prevention
   - Add alert on process open-fd counts or application EMFILE errors.
   - Add readiness probe tuning (longer timeout / failure threshold) temporarily to avoid flapping during start-up, but don't mask the underlying issue.

Commands I ran (so you can reproduce)
- Listed pods with readiness and image (filtered for ledger-api).
- kubectl describe pod <three failing pods> → showed readiness probe and events.
- kubectl describe deployment ledger-api → rollout events.
- kubectl get events -n ledger --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 100 → timeline of readiness failures and scaling.
- kubectl get nodes -o wide and kubectl describe node rcabench-worker2 → node is Ready and has capacity for pods.
- Fetched pod logs (last 30 minutes) from each failing pod filtered for errors — showed repeated "Too many open files" errors.

Investigation completeness and next checks
- Confirmed: EMFILE errors inside the application are the proximate cause of readiness failures and NotReady status for those pods on rcabench-worker2.
- Not yet confirmed: whether the root cause is an application-level FD leak introduced by 1.4.2 vs. a node-level ulimit/configuration difference. To decide:
  - Compare ulimit (ulimit -n) inside a healthy pod vs. failing pod.
  - Inspect image/entrypoint for changes in 1.4.2 that could open FDs or fail to close them.
  - Check how many sockets/files are open (ls /proc/1/fd) on failing pods.
  - If node-level, inspect node-level containerd/systemd LimitNOFILE and fs.file-max.

If you want I can:
- Run commands to check open-fd counts inside a failing pod and a healthy pod (kubectl exec).
- Show the exact events & timeline again or fetch logs from other pods for comparison.
- Prepare a suggested patch (Dockerfile/entrypoint change) and the cluster node-change steps to raise LimitNOFILE in containerd with exact commands.

Summary (one line)
- The ledger-api pods on rcabench-worker2 hit the process file-descriptor limit ("Too many open files") right after the 1.4.2 rollout, causing readiness probe failures and making 3 of 6 pods NotReady; remediate by restarting/rolling back pods and fix by addressing the FD limit or application FD leak.
